questions.question: What state shape does createEntityAdapter manage?
questions.explanation: The adapter stores an ordered ids array plus an entities lookup table keyed by id, and getInitialState can add extra fields like status.

questions.question: An employee with id E101 already exists. Which adapter method ignores a new object with id E101?
questions.explanation: addOne and addMany skip items whose id already exists. setOne replaces the item, upsertOne shallow-merges it, and setAll replaces the whole collection.

questions.question: You call upsertOne with { empCode: "E102", ctcLakh: 16 } for an existing entity that has a dept field. What happens to dept?
options: dept is removed because the new object does not have it
The call throws because dept is missing
dept is kept, because upsert shallow-merges into the existing entity
questions.explanation: upsertOne shallow-merges new fields into an existing entity, so fields not in the update stay as they were. setOne would replace the whole entity.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of normalising Redux state?
options: O(1) lookup of an item by id
Each item is stored once, so updates happen in one place
It removes the need for any selectors
Updating one item does not change unrelated item references
questions.explanation: Normalisation still relies on selectors; createEntityAdapter even generates them with getSelectors. The other three are genuine benefits.
